From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident logs and retention — immediate questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. We have an open incident that affected a small subset of Acme Health tenant traffic and our legal team has asked us to put a forensic hold on the related logs while they assess scope. Before we formally request a hold, can you confirm: 

- What is Redwood's standard post-incident retention window for request logs, request/response payloads, and KV/cache snapshots?
- Can you produce a time-stamped manifest and cryptographic hashes for any exported buckets?
- Are we able to request a temporary extended hold (beyond normal retention) and for how long?

We may need this preserved for up to 12 months depending on counsel. Appreciate a short write-up we can share with our L3.

Attachments: none on this email.

Best,
Samantha Cole
Security Operations Manager
Acme Health
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident logs and retention — immediate questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note. Summary answers below so you can share with counsel; I followed with internal ops next steps.

Short answers (summary):
- Default retention: request logs and metadata = 90 days; full request/response payloads (when stored) = 90 days.
- Extended hold: we can implement a forensics hold up to 365 days on a per-incident basis with approval (longer by exec/legal exception).
- Manifest/hashes: yes — we provide a CSV manifest and SHA256 hashes for exported archives, plus a signed timestamp from our KMS.

Recommended initial approach:
1) Put a provisional 180-day hold on all artifacts (captures, request traces, KV snapshots) to give Acme counsel time to triage.
2) Our forensics team will produce: manifest + SHA256 for each archive, MD5 for quick lookup, and a short summary doc describing sampling methodology.
3) If counsel requires, request an extension to 365 days; we will route through legal for the exec exception.

I can execute the provisional 180-day hold today if you confirm the scope (time window and tenant IDs). If you want us to include any particular correlation keys (user IDs, session ids), list them and we will slice accordingly.

Next steps (internal): I am going to loop in Forensics and Legal for chain-of-custody and export process.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick operational/ legal plan below, happy to iterate.

Operational preservation (what we'll do now):
- Scope: preserve all request traces and stored payloads for tenant IDs provided by Acme for the window 2028-03-12T22:10:00Z to 2028-03-12T24:00:00Z (we'll confirm exact timestamps from their list).
- Slicing: export full traces plus KV snapshots at t0, t0+30m, end-of-window. Also include a 1% random sample of surrounding traffic for context.
- Retention: set a hold of 180 days by default (applies to exported artifacts and internal archives).
- Hashing/manifest: generate a CSV manifest with filename, byte-size, SHA256 hash, KMS-signed timestamp; include an HMAC over the manifest signed with Redwood HSM key.

Legal/approval:
- Laura: please confirm whether we need an exec-level exception for a 365-day hold. My read: 365 days for regulated PHI cases should be routable via standard legal approval and a signed hold form; exec exception only if >365 days.
- Acme counsel (Mandi Law): we'll provide the manifest and an explanation of our export process. If you require an formal chain-of-custody affidavit, we can provide one within 3 business days.

Next steps / action items:
1) Tessa: collect and send exact tenant IDs + correlation keys (user/session ids) from Acme.
2) Rishi/Forensics: prepare export and manifest; target ETA for initial export = 24 hours after tenant IDs received.
3) Laura: confirm legal wording and whether an exec exception is required for 365 days; advise on any additional evidence certification.
4) Samantha/Acme: confirm you want the 180-day provisional hold or request immediate 365-day hold.

Attachments: acme_evidence_manifest.csv (template), incident_summary_ACME.docx (export notes).

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Forensics & Incident Response
Redwood Inference
